newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Burundi sanctions summit postponed until April 14.
newsitem.headline: Burundi sanctions summit postponed until April 14.

text.p: A regional summit on sanctions to force Burundi's rulers to talk to Hutu rebels has been postponed until April 14, a Tanzanian official said on Thursday.
The foreign ministry official said the summit, scheduled for April 8 in the northern Tanzanian town of Arusha, was postponed as leaders have other commitments, including a regional economic meeting.
Regional sanctions were imposed on Burundi last July after the Tutsi-dominated army seized power from a Hutu civilian president and replaced him with Tutsi retired major Pierre Buyoya.
Sanctions have so far failed to force Buyoya to open negotiations with rebels of the Hutu majority, who are fighting for a greater political say in the tiny central African state.
In his latest report, U.N. Special Rapporteur for Human Rights Paulo Pinheiro said in February "there is no sign of the beginnings of a Burundi strategy for peace and reconciliation".
More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and fighting between the army and rebels since the killing of Burundi's first elected Hutu president Melchior Ndadaye in October 1993.
At a meeting on sanctions in October regional leaders said they were not satisfied progress had been made and maintained the embargo. Buyoya last month said sanctions were killing the peace process.
